method: Question prompts, options and transfer prompts were extracted without candidate answer indices or explanations. The following answers were derived before inspecting the candidate key, guide or tests.

answers.work: At x=2, y-hat=5; residual=4-5=-1. Transfer y=7 gives residual2 and squared residual4.
(-2)^2+1^2+3^2=4+1+9=14. Reversing all signs preserves each square, so SSE remains14.
Residuals1,-1 sum to0 but SSE=2. Under y-hat=-x, fitted values1,-1 equal the observations, both residuals are0 and SSE=0.

OLS squares y_i-(a+b*x_i) at the same x. For(2,5), y-hat=x gives vertical residual3 and square9. Perpendicular distance is3/sqrt(2), square9/2; that geometric loss has a slope-dependent scaling and is a different fitting criterion.
D=3*8=24 and slope numerator=3*8=24, so b=1,a=2/3. Residuals1/3,-2/3,1/3 give SSE2/3. Changing the middle y to2 keeps sum(xy)=8 but mean(y)=4/3: a=4/3,b=1; residuals-1/3,2/3,-1/3 and SSE2/3.
The intercept normal equation forces a+b*mean(x)=mean(y), hence (3/2,3). Adding5 to x moves it to(13/2,3); b is unchanged and a changes to a-5b.
SSE2/3 is the minimum among all lines but cannot make non-collinear observations exact. Adding10 to every y adds10 to the intercept, preserving all fitted residuals and minimum SSE2/3.

For(0,0),(0,2),(2,2), D=8 and slope numerator4, so a=1,b=1/2,SSE2. Removing(2,2) leaves shared x0 and mean y1: a=1 is determined, b arbitrary, predicted value at x0 is1, minimum SSE2, other-x predictions undetermined.
Adding7 to y changes a from2/3 to23/3; b=1 and SSE2/3 remain. With x'=x+5, substitute x=x'-5 to obtain y-hat=8/3+x'.
Substitute x=x'/2 into2/3+x to get2/3+x'/2. SSE stays2/3 because all fitted y values and vertical residuals at corresponding observations are unchanged.

Repeating every row twice multiplies the objective by2 without changing its minimizer: a=2/3,b=1,SSE4/3. Tripling every row gives the same coefficients and SSE2. Copying existing records does not establish new independent observations.

For the four rows, sum x13,sum y-7,sum x²105,sum xy-95. D=251,slope numerator-289, so b=-289/251,a=500/251. Residuals(-500,40,580,-120)/251 give SSE2400/251. Changing the last row to(10,10) puts every point on y=x, so a=0,b=1,SSE0. A distant x need not change a line when its y lies on that line.

At shared x3, fit the constant predicted value to mean y3. Residuals-2,0,2 give SSE8 and family a+3b=3. At x4, minimizing lines(0,1) and(3,0) predict4 and3, respectively, proving non-identification there.
At x3, fitted11/3 lies outside the observed x range[-2,2], so it is extrapolation. At x1, fitted5/3 is in range but neither observation accuracy nor a future outcome is guaranteed.

SSE0 describes the recorded pairs but does not identify an intervention effect. A latent common cause can drive both variables; design, timing, measurement and a defensible causal identification strategy such as appropriate randomization would provide additional information.

The best line y=2 has residuals2,-1,-2,-1,2 and SSE14. The authored curve y=x² has zero in-sample residuals and SSE0. This describes a sample pattern and does not establish a causal mechanism or out-of-sample accuracy.
